title: Recruiter and Assessment Patterns
tagline: Year 4 — Reading an official assessment notice and turning it into a plan: sections, time, marks, penalties and cutoffs

introduction.overview: Every assessment has a pattern: the sections, the number of questions, the time allowed, whether time is per section or overall, the marks and the penalty. These details change from company to company and from year to year, so this chapter gives no company-specific figures. It teaches how to read an official notice, extract the pattern into a one-page plan, and compute what it implies: time per question, marks per minute, the attempts needed to meet a stated cutoff, and the effect of the penalty rule.
introduction.placementRelevance: Knowing the exact pattern lets you plan pacing and selection instead of guessing.
introduction.realWorldContext: Reading terms, rules and specifications before starting work is a professional habit.

learningObjectives: Extract a pattern from an official notice
Compute time per question for each section
Compute marks needed for a stated cutoff
Reflect the penalty rule in strategy
Identify what to confirm with the recruiter

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Time per question = section time ÷ questions. Marks needed = cutoff percentage × total marks.

coreDefinitions: Pattern: the structure of an assessment.
Sectional timer: time is fixed per section.
Overall timer: one clock for the whole test.
Cutoff: the minimum score to pass a stage.
Official notice: the instructions from the employer or test provider.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: The pattern is the rulebook of the game. Read it before playing.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Write one line per section: questions, minutes, marks, penalty. Then compute pace and cutoffs.

mainNarrative: Suppose a (hypothetical) notice says: Aptitude 20 questions in 25 minutes, Reasoning 15 questions in 20 minutes, Verbal 25 questions in 20 minutes, each question 1 mark, 0.25 penalty. The paces are 75 s, 80 s and 48 s per question.
Total marks 60; a 60% cutoff needs 36 net marks.
With 90% accuracy and a 0.25 penalty, each attempt nets 0.9 − 0.025 = 0.875 marks, so 36 net marks need about 36 ÷ 0.875 = 41 attempts.
Confirm with the recruiter: whether sectional timers apply, whether you can go back, and the exact penalty.
Never rely on an unofficial claim about a pattern; patterns change.

deepDiveAspects.title: Sectional timers
deepDiveAspects.content: With sectional timers you cannot move time between sections, so plan each section separately.

deepDiveAspects.title: Cutoff stages
deepDiveAspects.content: Some tests have sectional cutoffs as well as an overall cutoff; check both.

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Write the official pattern in one line per section, compute paces and cutoffs, and confirm unclear points with the recruiter.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Use the pattern to decide guessing.
placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Keep a one-page pattern sheet per company.
